pages.text:
Comprehensive management of
patients with diabetes and CKD Regular
risk factor
a. Goals of care (progression, CVD reduction)
b. Imperative for addressing multiple risk reassessment
factors and combination treatments (every 3–6
c. Focus on evidence-based therapies that
improve clinical outcomes/organ protection months)
d. Self-management
e. Systems approaches
Goals Pharmacologic therapies
Lifestyle interventions
It’s not just about glucose! First-line therapies
• Consume diet high in vegetables, fruits,
whole grains, plant-based proteins 1 Promote self-management
• For patients not on dialysis, aim for 0.8 g and team-based integrated
protein/kg weight per day Metformin SGLT2 inhibitors RAS inhibitors Statins
care (T2D, eGFR ≥30) (T2D, eGFR ≥20) (HTN)
• For patients on dialysis, aim for 1.0–1.2 g
protein/kg weight per day 2 Use organ-protective therapies Additional drugs for heart and kidney protection
• Limit sodium intake <2 g/day (<5 g NaCl) 3 Treat multiple targets
• Exercise for at least 150 min per week (glycemia, BP, lipids, UACR,
• Stop tobacco use
eGFR) GLP-1 RA ns-MRA Antiplatelet therapies
• Manage weight
(T2D) (T2D) (ASCVD)
Glycemic monitoring and targets
• Use HbA1c to monitor glycemic control
• Individualize HbA1c targets (< 6.5% to < 8.0%)
based on patient comorbidities, hypoglycemia
risk, resources and preferences
• Use CGM or SMBG when treatment associated
with risk of hypoglycemia or when HbA1c is
not concordant with blood glucose
< 6.5% HbA1c < 8.0%
Coordinated care
Abbreviations: ASCVD, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease; BP, blood pressure; CGM, continuous glucose monitoring; CKD, chronic kidney disease; CVD, cardiovascular disease; eGFR, estimated glomerular
filtration rate; GLP-1, glucagon-like peptide-1; HbA1c, glycated hemoglobin; NaCl, sodium chloride; RAS, renin-angiotensin system; SGLT2, sodium-glucose cotransporter-2; SMBG, self-monitoring of blood
glucose; T2D, type 2 diabetes; UACR, urine albumin-creatinine ratio
